requirement: Apply user edits to a frozen profile by producing a new, fully validated profile with a bumped version, refusing edits to non-editable fields and returning the same object when nothing changes.
skeleton: A frozen extra-forbid Profile model with Field bounds, an EDITABLE frozenset, and apply_update checking unknown keys, short-circuiting empty changes, and re-validating a dumped and updated dict with an incremented version.
caption: Editing a frozen pydantic v2 model so the result is validated exactly like a freshly constructed one. Profile sets ConfigDict with frozen and extra forbid, and has handle with Field min_length=3 and max_length=15, display_name with min_length=1 and max_length=50, tags as a tuple of str defaulting to empty, and version defaulting to 1 with ge=1. Assigning to a field of a frozen model raises pydantic.ValidationError. EDITABLE is a frozenset of display_name and tags. apply_update(profile, changes) first computes the change keys outside EDITABLE and raises ValueError listing them sorted and comma-separated after fields not editable. An empty change mapping returns the same profile object. Otherwise it takes model_dump of the profile, updates that dict with the changes, sets version to the old version plus one and passes the dict to model_validate, because model_copy with update skips validation and coercion entirely. The fixture asserts that renaming returns a new profile at version 2 while the original is untouched, that an empty or 51-character display name raises ValidationError, that a tags list is coerced to a tuple, that editing version and handle raises ValueError reading fields not editable: handle, version, that an empty update returns the identical object, and that assignment on a profile raises ValidationError.

constraints: Edits produce a new profile and leave the original unchanged
Every edit bumps the version by one
Edited values are validated and coerced
Editing fields outside display_name and tags raises ValueError
An empty edit returns the same object
Profiles cannot be mutated in place

rationale.teaches: Re-validating model_dump plus changes through model_validate, since model_copy(update=...) bypasses validation on pydantic models.
rationale.why: model_copy looks like the obvious immutable update, but it lets invalid and uncoerced values into a model everyone assumes was validated.

ops.docstring: Apply user edits to a frozen profile model without skipping validation.

ops.stmt: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

ops.source:
class Profile(BaseModel):
    """A public user profile; instances never change after validation."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")

    handle: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=15)
    display_name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=50)
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    version: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)

candidates.why_wrong: model_copy with update skips validation, so empty names and uncoerced lists get in.
Any field, including handle and version, can be overwritten by an edit.
The version is copied instead of incremented after an edit.
An empty edit creates a new object and bumps the version anyway.
The check is inverted, refusing editable fields and allowing the rest.
